delta: # Story 88 — PORTAL-

2-WEB customer signs in and sees only their tickets (Story: CRM-122)

## Prerequisites

- **`CUSTOMERS-6-API (CRM-65)` must be
merged first.** Until then `api/src/features/tickets/tickets.service.js` still refuses every subject whose role is `customer` outright (
see the comment in that file); a portal built over that guard would 404 its own users. Confirm the guard has become a comparison (customer may read

tickets they own) before starting execution.
- **`TICKETS-8-API` must be merged first** — a customer asking for someone else's ticket must receive the same

404 a missing ticket gets, and asking for the queue must be refused. That contract is what the WEB story leans on.
- No
prior plan exists under `.squad/plans/portal/`; this is the first plan in the folder. Match the tone and structure of sibling `tickets`

/ `customers` plans if any exist by the time execution starts.
- Coordination: no `api/` changes are permitted here. If an API refusal is missing,

raise a finding — do not patch it in this story.

---

## Story Goal

A signed-in customer lands on **their own tickets** and nothing else. The des
k shell they see has **no staff link** — no *Home* dashboard, no *Customers*, no *Queue*, no staff *Raise a ticket*. Reading a ticket that
is theirs works; reading one that is not returns the same 404 a missing ticket returns. Staff (agent, admin) experience is **un

changed** — the queue, the customer list, and every staff screen behave exactly as before.

Explicitly **not** in scope: ticket replies, internal-note vis

ibility (PORTAL-3-WEB), reopening, rating, knowledge-base articles, and **any change under `api/`**.

---

## Context — Read These Files First

1. `web
/src/shared/session/use-me.ts` — **read the whole file**. Confirms the shape `Me = { id: string; role: string; name: string }` (line 29) and the ex
ported helpers `isAdmin` / `isStaff` on `useMe()` (lines 46–47: `data.role === 'admin'`, `data.role !== 'customer'`). The r

est of this story keys off `isStaff` / `role === 'customer'`.
2. `web/src/app/routes.tsx` — read the whole file. Note the current route table

(from grep):
   - `/sign-in`, `/raise` (public)
   - `/` (Home), `/customers`, `/customers/new`, `/customers/:id`

- `/tickets`, `/tickets/new`
   - `/account/password`, `/accounts/set-password`
   - `*` → `Navigate to="/"`
   Line ~111 already
contains a comment explaining that a router-level role gate is a lie and that **the API is the enforcement (SC-2)** — read that comment before ad
ding any client-side gate; the plan below respects it (the shell hides links, the API ref

uses calls, and the router does not pretend to enforce).
3. `web/src/app/desk-shell/DeskShell.tsx` — read the whole file. The nav lists **
Home, Customers, The queue, Raise a ticket** — all staff screens. This story teaches the shell that there are two audiences. Also read

`DeskShell.test.tsx` to match its test style.
4. `web/src/pages/tickets/TicketQueuePage.tsx` — read the whole file. This is the **pa
ging and empty-state precedent** (BR-4 pagination, D-2 empty state). Take its pagination and its "empty says

so" state; **do not** take its assign / status controls (out of scope for a customer).
5. `web/src/pages/tickets/useTicketQueue.ts` — read to see
how the queue is fetched, paginated, and how filter params are passed. The customer version will call the same tickets endpoint but sc

oped to the caller (the API scopes it by subject; the client sends no extra filter).
6. `web/src/pages/tickets/TicketQueuePage

.test.tsx` — read to match the test patterns (mocked `useRequest` responses, paging assertions, empty-state assertion).
7. `web/src/shared/api/client.ts` — read

(small file) to see how request URLs are formed. Confirms the client sends session cookies so the API can identify the customer.
8. `web/src/
shared/i18n/en.ts` and `web/src/shared/i18n/ar.ts` — read the whole files. Every user-facing string in the new page and

the customer shell must be a key present in **both** files (BR-6, L-30, L-51). See `parity.test.ts` for how parity is enforced.
9. `web/src/pages
/sign-in/SignInPage.tsx` — read the whole file. Confirms where the "post sign-in redirect" is decided (this story changes that

decision to depend on role).
10. `web/src/pages/sign-in/SignInPage.test.tsx` — read; the redirect assertion is here

today and must be **duplicated for a customer sign-in** case.
11. `web/src/app/require-auth.tsx` — read (small).

Confirms the gate that already runs before the shell mounts.
12. `web/src/pages/portal/PublicRaiseTicketPage.tsx` — sibling for tone; the custom

er-facing shell should feel like this page, not like the desk.
13. `api/src/features/tickets/tickets.service.js` — **read the customer bran
ch only.** Confirm (do not modify) that a `customer` subject reading a ticket that is not theirs receives the **same 404** as a missing
ticket, and that queue / assignee-list / other-customer calls are refused with 403 or 404. If any of those has not yet landed, st

op and file a finding rather than proceed. Grep for `role === 'customer'` and `throw` in that file.
14. `api/src/features/customers/customers.service.js` and `api/src/features/identity/identity.service.js

` — grep for the customer-refusal branches so the web tests mock the same status codes the API actually returns.
15. `.squad/plan-lessons.md` — read

before writing any code. One rule per prior review defect; a plan that repeats a listed defect is rejected in review.
16. `docs/taxonomy.

md`, `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/git.md` — cite, do not restate.
17. `scripts/criteria/portal.md` — PORTAL-2-WEB (line 52). Verify the acceptance criteria have

not shifted since intake.

---

## Product rules (from story)

- **Current:** After sign-in every user lands on `/` (the desk

Home), and the shell shows *Home, Customers, The queue, Raise a ticket* regardless of role.
- **New:** After sign-in, a subject whose `role === 'customer'` lands on **`/my/
tickets`** and sees a shell whose navigation contains **only** *My tickets* and *Sign out* (plus *Change password* if that is where it already l

ives). Agents and admins are **unchanged** — same landing (`/`), same nav, same behaviour.

Enforcement split

(SC-2):
- The **shell hides staff links** from customers, because showing them would be a lie — but that is **presentation**, not enforcement.
- The **API ref
uses** every customer call to queue, staff list, or another customer; the web story does not add a client-side gate. See the com

ment already in `routes.tsx` ~line 111.

---

## Frontend Tasks

### 1 — Teach the session hook to distinguish audiences

**

File:** `web/src/shared/session/use-me.ts`

The hook already exposes `isAdmin` and `isStaff`. Add a third derived flag `isCustomer` alongside them, mirrored on the same object

:

```ts
isCustomer: data ? data.role === 'customer' : undefined,
```

Do **not** change the shape of `Me` or the API response contract. `isCustomer === undefined` while
`data` is loading — every consumer must treat `undefined` as "not yet known" (render nothing / a skeleton), the same way `isStaff` is already tre

ated.

### 2 — Route the customer to their tickets after sign-in

**File:** `web/src/pages/sign-in/SignInPage.tsx`

Where the

page currently redirects on success, branch on the fresh session's role:

- `role === 'customer'` → `navigate('/my/tickets', {

replace: true })`
- anything else → the **existing** redirect (unchanged).

Fetch the role from the same source the shell will use (the `useMe` refetch after sign-in),
not from the sign-in response body — one source of truth. Do **not** hard-code the customer path
anywhere else; export a constant `CUSTOMER_HOME = '/my/tickets'` from a small `

web/src/pages/portal/routes.ts` and import it in both the sign-in page and the router.

### 3 — Add the customer routes and a router-level fallback

**File:** `

web/src/app/routes.tsx`

Add two new authenticated routes:

- `/my/tickets` → `<MyTicketsPage />` (Story 88, this

story)
- `/my/tickets/:id` → `<MyTicketDetailPage />` (this story — read-only view of one owned ticket)

Do **not** add a role g
ate in the router. Keep — verbatim — the existing comment near line 111 that explains why (SC-2). If, and only if, a customer lands
on `/`, `/tickets`, `/customers`, `/customers/*`, or `/tickets/new`, the shell renders — the API refuses their calls, and the empty page sh

ows the same error state a refused request always shows. This is deliberate: the API is the enforcement.

Do **not** touch the `*` fallback
; `Navigate to="/"` is fine for both audiences (a customer redirected to `/` sees a shell with no staff links and no

data — a dead end, matching the "no confirmation of anything they cannot have" rule).

### 4 — Give the shell two

navigations (one shell, role-branched)

**File:** `web/src/app/desk-shell/DeskShell.tsx`

Choose one shell, branch on role. **Rationale (write
this as a comment in the file):** a second shell duplicates the header, the language switch, the sign-out button, and the account
-password link — four surfaces that must stay in sync. One shell with a role-branched nav keeps the pinned staff experience liter

ally the same component.

Change:

1. Call `useMe()` at the top of `DeskShell`.
2. While `isCustomer === undefined && isStaff === undefined`, render the

existing skeleton (do not flash the staff nav to a customer).
3. When `isCustomer === true`, render **only** the *My tickets* link (

and *Change password* / *Sign out* if those live in this shell today — grep to confirm).
4. When `isCustomer === false` (i.e. `isStaff === true`), render the **existing** n
av exactly as it is today. **Do not** re-order, rename, or re-key any staff link — a rename would fail `DeskShell.test.tsx` and would

break muscle memory for agents.

**Do not** add a customer-only class name to the shell root that chang

es staff styling. The staff branch must be byte-identical output when the role is not customer.

### 5 — Build the customer's *

My tickets* page

**Create file:** `web/src/pages/portal/MyTicketsPage.tsx`

Behaviour, mirroring `TicketQueuePage.tsx` (paging + empty state) but stripped of sta

ff controls:

- Fetch tickets via a new hook `useMyTickets` (see task 6). The API scopes by subject — the client

sends no `assignee`, no `status filter`, no `customer` param.
- Render a table / list of the customer's tickets.
Columns: reference / subject, status, updated-at. **No** assign control, **no** change-status control, **no** intern

al-note affordance.
- **Pagination** (BR-4): reuse the paging component `TicketQueuePage` uses. Same page size, same "next / previ

ous", same URL-query wiring (`?page=`).
- **Empty state** (D-2): "You have no tickets yet." (i

18n key `portal.myTickets.empty`). Do not render blank.
- **Error state:** on a 403 or 404 from the API (should not happen for the ca

ller's own list, but a mis-routed call could), render the shared `ErrorState` with a generic message; do **not** surface which resource was refused.
- Every
string comes from `en.ts` / `ar.ts` (BR-6). No inline literal strings — `no-hardcoded-strings.test.ts` will catch

this.

**Create file:** `web/src/pages/portal/MyTicketDetailPage.tsx`

- Reads `:id` from the URL and fetches `GET /tickets/:id`.
- On 404 (API retur
ns 404 for both missing and not-yours — see acceptance), render the shared `EmptyState` with a message that does **not** say "not
yours"; the message must be the same one a missing ticket produces. Suggested key: `portal.ticketDetail.notFound` = "This ticket could not be found." Same string in en

and ar.
- Renders only the ticket's own fields (subject, description, status, created-at, updated-at, category if the API returns it). **Does not** render the conversation, replies, internal notes, or assignee —

those are PORTAL-3-WEB.

**Create file:** `web/src/pages/portal/MyTicketsPage.css` — only if styles are need

ed beyond what `TicketQueuePage` reuses. Prefer reusing existing tokens (`web/src/shared/ui/tokens.css`).

### 6 — Data

hooks for the customer

**Create file:** `web/src/pages/portal/useMyTickets.ts`

- Wraps `useRequest` (see `web/src/shared/hooks/useRequest.ts` for the p

attern).
- Signature: `useMyTickets({ page }: { page: number })`.
- Calls the **same** `GET /tickets` endpoint the queue uses. **
Do not** invent a `/my/tickets` endpoint on the client — the API scopes by session subject already (see `tickets.service.js`). If

a separate endpoint turns out to be needed, that is an API change and belongs to a different story; **file a finding**.
- Returns `{
tickets, page, pageSize, total, isLoading, error }` — same shape `useTicketQueue` returns, minus any staff-only fields,

so the paging component can be reused unchanged.

**Create file:** `web/src/pages/portal/useMyTicket.ts`

- `useMyTicket(id: string)` → `GET /tickets/:id`,

returns `{ ticket, isLoading, error }`. Error carries the HTTP status so the page can render the shared 404 empty state.

### 7 — i18n

**Files:** `web/src/sh

ared/i18n/en.ts` and `web/src/shared/i18n/ar.ts`

Add keys, in both files, at parity. Suggested nesting (gr

ep the existing files for the closest existing shape and match it):

- `portal.nav.myTickets` — en: "My tickets", ar: "تذا

كري"
- `portal.myTickets.title` — en: "My tickets", ar: "تذاكري"
- `portal.myTickets.empty` — en: "You have no tickets yet.", ar: "لا تو

جد لديك تذاكر بعد."
- `portal.myTickets.columns.subject` / `.status` / `.updatedAt`
- `portal.ticketDetail

.title`
- `portal.ticketDetail.notFound` — en: "This ticket could not be found.", ar: (parallel Arabic)
- `portal.ticketDetail.field.subject` / `.description` / `.

status` / `.createdAt` / `.updatedAt` / `.category`

`parity.test.ts` (`web/src/shared/i18n/parity.test.ts`) must pass; keys added only to `

en` will fail it. `no-mirrored-styles.test.ts` and `no-hardcoded-strings.test.ts` apply.

---

## Backend Tasks
**No backend changes required.** The API contract this page depends on is delivered by `CUSTOMERS-6-API (CRM-65)` and `TICKETS-8-API`. If the API
refuses something it should not, or leaks the existence of a ticket that is not the caller's, that is a **

finding** to raise — not a change to make in this story.

---

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Role loading race.** `useMe()` returns `role
=== undefined` while loading. `DeskShell` must render its skeleton in that window — never the staff nav — otherwise a customer flashes staff links on every

reload. Enforced in `DeskShell.tsx` in task 4.
- **Customer types `/tickets` in the URL bar.** Router happily
mounts `TicketQueuePage`; the API refuses `GET /tickets?queue=…` for a
customer. Page renders its existing `ErrorState`. **Do not** add a client redirect — SC-2. Add a test that

this does not crash.
- **Customer opens `/customers/:id` for their own record.** The API decision

belongs to CUSTOMERS-6-API; this story does not gate it. Whatever the API returns, the page renders the appropriate state.
- **Customer opens `/my/tickets/:
id` for a ticket that is not theirs.** API returns 404 (per TICKETS-8-API acceptance). Page renders the same empty state a missing ticket renders. The message must be indistinguishable — en

forced by a test in task Test Plan #4.
- **Empty ticket list.** `MyTicketsPage` renders `portal.myTickets.empty`

, not a blank table (D-2). Test in Test Plan #2.
- **Pagination past the last page.** Same behaviour as `TicketQueuePage

` — clamp to the last page or show empty state. Reuse the queue's behaviour, do not diverge.
- **Sign out from the

customer shell.** The existing sign-out button must remain reachable. Verify it works from `/my/tickets`.
- **Language switch while on the customer shell.** `useF
ormatters` and the i18n context must switch dates and numbers in the ticket list just like they do in the desk. Cov

ered by BR-6.
- **Staff impersonation / role change mid-session.** Out of scope; `useMe` is refetched on navigation via exist

ing patterns.
- **A user with an unknown role (neither `customer`, `agent`, `admin`).** Treat as non
-customer (staff shell). Document this in a comment on the shell's role branch and assert with a test that an

unknown role does **not** see the customer shell.

---

## Test Plan

All web tests. Match the patterns in `TicketQueuePage.test.tsx`, `

DeskShell.test.tsx`, `SignInPage.test.tsx`.

1. **`web/src/pages/sign-in/SignInPage.test.tsx`** — add a case: sign in as a subject whose `me` returns `

role: 'customer'`; assert the redirect target is `/my/tickets`. Keep the existing agent / admin case unchanged (pins the staff half).
2. **`web/src/pages/portal/

MyTicketsPage.test.tsx`** (new) —
   - Renders the customer's tickets from a mocked `GET /tickets` response.
   - Renders the empty state (`portal.myTickets.empty`) when the response has

zero rows.
   - Renders pagination controls and advances `?page=` on next-click, matching `TicketQueuePage.test.ts

x`.
   - Renders an error state on a mocked 500.
   - Contains **no** assign / status / internal-note controls (assert by

`queryByRole` returning null).
3. **`web/src/pages/portal/MyTicketDetailPage.test.tsx`** (new) —
   - Renders a ticket's own fields on a 200.
   - Renders the shared "
not found" empty state on a 404, with a message equal to the string a missing ticket would show (parameterise the m

ock so the test proves the two paths produce the **same** DOM).
   - **Does not** render replies, notes, or an assignee.
4. **

`web/src/app/desk-shell/DeskShell.test.tsx`** — extend:
   - When `useMe()` returns `role: 'customer'`, the nav contains *My tickets* only;

grep-style assertions that *Home*, *Customers*, *The queue*, *Raise a ticket* are **absent**.
   - When `useMe()` returns `role:
'agent'` or `role: 'admin'`, the nav is byte-identical to today (snapshot or explicit link list —

pin the staff half).
   - When `useMe()` is still loading, neither nav is rendered.
5. **`web/src/pages/portal/portal-api-refus

al.test.tsx`** (new, SC-2 evidence) —
   - Mount `MyTicketsPage` with the API mocked to refuse `GET /tickets?queue=…`
, `GET /customers`, `GET /customers/:id`, and `GET /accounts` for a customer (whatever status codes the real API returns — grep `tickets.service.js` and `identity.service.js` for
the exact status). Assert the page still renders (does not crash) and shows an error state, and that the shell shows **no** link to those paths. The test's job is to prove the client does not

rely on link-absence for enforcement.
6. **`web/src/shared/i18n/parity.test.ts`** — passes with the new keys; no drift between `en` and `ar`

.
7. **`web/src/pages/no-hardcoded-strings.test.ts`** — passes with the new pages; every string is a key.
8. **`web/src/app/routing.test.tsx`** — extend to prove `/my/tickets

` and `/my/tickets/:id` mount their pages when authenticated.

---

## Verification Steps

1. **Frontend tests:** `cd web && np

m test` — all suites pass; new tests in tasks Test Plan #1–8 pass.
2. **Frontend build:** `cd web && npm run build` — `tsc -b && vite build` completes with no

type errors. (Reminder: `npm test` is vitest and does **not** typecheck; `npm run build` is the only real typecheck.)
3. **Backend tests un
changed:** `cd api && npm test` — every suite still passes; this story ships no `api/` diff, so the tree of api tests is identical to `

main`.
4. **Regression — staff pinning:** manually (or via the extended `DeskShell.test.tsx`) confirm agent and admin see the same nav and land at

`/` after sign-in.
5. **No AI attribution anywhere:** `git grep -iE 'co-authored-by:
.*(claude|copilot|gpt|assistant)|generated by (an )?ai|assisted by ai|ai-assisted

'` — must return **no matches** across the diff, including commit messages and any new files.
6. **Docs unchanged unless ta
xonomy demands it:** `git status docs/` — expect no modifications; if a new user-facing term was introduced, update `docs

/taxonomy.md` only.
7. **Manual smoke:** `cd api && npm run seed` then `cd api && npm start` (in one
shell) and `cd web && npm run dev` (in another). Sign in as a seeded customer → land on `/my/tickets`, see own tickets, see no staff links. Sign in as an agent → land on `/`, see

the queue unchanged. Try `/my/tickets/<some-other-customer's-ticket-id>` as a customer → same 404 empty state as a made-up id.

---
